name: Ammishaddai
overview: Ammishaddai was a male member of the tribe of Dan, known primarily as the father of Ahiezer. His mention in Scripture is brief and centers on his role within his family and tribal lineage, without additional notes or elaboration.
namesAndTitles: The name Ammishaddai means "Shaddai is [my] kinsman," indicating a connection or reliance on the Almighty God, Shaddai. This proper name, as recorded in Numbers 1:12, reflects a personal acknowledgment of God's protective relationship.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Ammishaddai as the father of Ahiezer and a descendant of the tribe of Dan. Beyond these relationships, no further family details are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Ammishaddai's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his identification as the father of Ahiezer, who is notable within the tribe of Dan. This connection situates Ammishaddai within the genealogical and tribal structure important to Israel's organization as recorded in Numbers 1:12, underscoring God's providential ordering of His people.
